You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0070.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

SetBondStereoFromDirections 
SetBondStereoFromDirections( (Mol)mol) -> None :
    Uses the directions of neighboring bonds to set cis/trans stereo on double bonds.
            
      ARGUMENTS:
      
        - mol: the molecule to be modified
    
    

    C++ signature :
        void SetBondStereoFromDirections(RDKit::ROMol {lvalue})
AssignStereochemistry 
AssignStereochemistry( (Mol)mol [, (bool)cleanIt=False [, (bool)force=False [, (bool)flagPossibleStereoCenters=False]]]) -> None :
    Assign stereochemistry tags to atoms and bonds.
      If useLegacyStereoPerception is true, it also does the CIP stereochemistry
      assignment for the molecule's atoms (R/S) and double bonds (Z/E).
      This assignment is based on legacy code which is fast, but is
      known to incorrectly assign CIP labels in some cases.
      instead, to assign CIP labels based on an accurate, though slower,
      implementation of the CIP rules, call CIPLabeler::assignCIPLabels().
      Chiral atoms will have a property '_CIPCode' indicating their chiral code.
    
      ARGUMENTS:
    
        - mol: the molecule to use
        - cleanIt: (optional) if provided, any existing values of the property `_CIPCode`
            will be cleared, atoms with a chiral specifier that aren't
          actually chiral (e.g. atoms with duplicate substituents or only 2 substituents,
          etc.) will have their chiral code set to CHI_UNSPECIFIED. Bonds with 
          STEREOCIS/STEREOTRANS specified that have duplicate substituents based upon the CIP 
          atom ranks will be marked STEREONONE. 
        - force: (optional) causes the calculation to be repeated, even if it has already
          been done
        - flagPossibleStereoCenters (optional)   set the _ChiralityPossible property on
          atoms that are possible stereocenters
    

    C++ signature :
        void AssignStereochemistry(RDKit::ROMol {lvalue} [,bool=False [,bool=False [,bool=False]]])

SetDoubleBondNeighborDirections( (Mol)mol [, (object)conf=None]) -> None :

cat > build.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem, rdMolDescriptors
from rdkit.Geometry import Point3D
import numpy as np
# Atom labels and 2D drawing positions (image y inverted below).
data=[
('C','acidC',205,404),('O','acid=O',165,337),('O','acidOH',145,445),
('C','alpha',309,344),('C','alphaMe',309,230),('C','beta',413,404),
('C','gamma',517,344),('C','delta',623,404),('C','A',724,344),
('C','A-Me',724,472),('O','lactO',724,226),('C','lactC',828,164),
('O','lact=O',828,48),('C','B',932,223),('C','E',855,240),
('C','F',809,315),('C','D',828,404),('C','C',932,344),
('C','G',1025,149),('C','H',1142,176),('C','I',1194,283),
('C','J',1142,392),('C','K',1026,418),('C','esterC',1314,283),
('O','ester=O',1364,188),('O','esterO',1374,387),('C','esterMe',1494,387),
('O','acetO',932,457),('C','acetC',1036,517),('O','acet=O',1036,637),('C','acetMe',1140,457)]
bonds=[(0,1,2),(0,2,1),(0,3,1),(3,4,1),(3,5,2),(5,6,1),(6,7,2),(7,8,1),
(8,9,1),(8,10,1),(10,11,1),(11,12,2),(11,13,1),(13,14,1),(14,15,1),(16,15,1),
(16,8,1),(16,17,1),(17,13,1),(13,18,1),(18,19,1),(19,20,2),(20,21,1),(21,22,1),(22,17,1),
(20,23,1),(23,24,2),(23,25,1),(25,26,1),(17,27,1),(27,28,1),(28,29,2),(28,30,1)]
rw=Chem.RWMol()
for elem,label,x,y in data:
 a=Chem.Atom(elem); a.SetProp('_Name',label); rw.AddAtom(a)
for i,j,n in bonds: rw.AddBond(i,j,Chem.BondType.DOUBLE if n==2 else Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
m=rw.GetMol(); Chem.SanitizeMol(m)
conf=Chem.Conformer(len(data)); conf.Set3D(False)
for i,(_,_,x,y) in enumerate(data): conf.SetAtomPosition(i,Point3D(x/100,-y/100,0))
m.AddConformer(conf)
for i,j,d in [(8,9,Chem.BondDir.BEGINDASH),(13,14,Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE),(16,15,Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE),(17,27,Chem.BondDir.BEGINWEDGE)]:
 m.GetBondBetweenAtoms(i,j).SetBondDir(d)
Chem.AssignChiralTypesFromBondDirs(m)
for i,j,k,l in [(3,5,0,6),(6,7,5,8)]:
 b=m.GetBondBetweenAtoms(i,j);b.SetStereoAtoms(k,l);b.SetStereo(Chem.BondStereo.STEREOE)
b=m.GetBondBetweenAtoms(19,20);b.SetStereoAtoms(18,21);b.SetStereo(Chem.BondStereo.STEREOZ)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(m,cleanIt=True,force=True)
print('SMILES:',Chem.MolToSmiles(m))
print('Formula:',rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula(m))
for a in m.GetAtoms():
 if a.GetChiralTag()!=Chem.ChiralType.CHI_UNSPECIFIED: print(a.GetIdx(),a.GetProp('_Name'),a.GetChiralTag(),a.GetProp('_CIPCode') if a.HasProp('_CIPCode') else '')
Chem.MolToMolFile(m,'drawing.mol')
# use canonical stereochemical SMILES to clear 2D directions but retain atom ordering
for b in m.GetBonds(): b.SetBondDir(Chem.BondDir.NONE)
m.RemoveAllConformers(); m=Chem.AddHs(m)
p=AllChem.ETKDGv3();p.randomSeed=70007;p.numThreads=4
ids=AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(m, numConfs=100, params=p)
print('Conformers:',len(ids))
res=AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(m,numThreads=4,maxIters=2500)
best=min(range(len(res)),key=lambda i:res[i][1]);cid=int(ids[best]);print('Best',cid,res[best])
Chem.MolToXYZFile(m,'answer.xyz',confId=cid)
Chem.MolToMolFile(m,'answer.sdf',confId=cid)
# validate stereochemistry from coordinates
check=Chem.Mol(m);Chem.AssignStereochemistryFrom3D(check,confId=cid,replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(check,force=True,cleanIt=True)
for i in [8,13,16,17]: print('3D stereo',i,check.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetProp('_CIPCode'),'expected',m.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetProp('_CIPCode'))
np.save('coords.npy',np.array(m.GetConformer(cid).GetPositions()))
PY
python build.py

cat > verify.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import rdMolTransforms
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
m=Chem.MolFromMolFile('answer.sdf',removeHs=False)
xyz=Path('xtb_refine/xtbopt.xyz')
assert xyz.exists()
lines=xyz.read_text().splitlines();n=int(lines[0]);assert n==m.GetNumAtoms()==59
coords=np.array([[float(t) for t in s.split()[1:4]] for s in lines[2:2+n]])
for i,p in enumerate(coords):
 assert lines[i+2].split()[0]==m.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetSymbol()
 m.GetConformer().SetAtomPosition(i,p)
Chem.AssignStereochemistryFrom3D(m,replaceExistingTags=True)
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(m,cleanIt=True,force=True)
for i,label in [(8,'R'),(13,'R'),(16,'S'),(17,'S')]:
 obs=m.GetAtomWithIdx(i).GetProp('_CIPCode');assert obs==label,(i,obs,label)
for ids in [(0,3,5,6),(5,6,7,8)]:
 angle=rdMolTransforms.GetDihedralDeg(m.GetConformer(),*ids); print(ids,angle); assert abs(angle)>160
for b in m.GetBonds():
 d=np.linalg.norm(coords[b.GetBeginAtomIdx()]-coords[b.GetEndAtomIdx()]);assert 0.8<d<1.8,(b.GetIdx(),d)
Chem.MolToXYZFile(m,'answer.xyz')
p=Path('answer.xyz');ls=p.read_text().splitlines();ls[1]='C23H28O8; stereochemistry from mol_0070.png; GFN2-xTB optimized; angstrom'
p.write_text('\n'.join(ls)+'\n')
print('Confirmed answer.xyz:',p.resolve(),'atoms',n)
PY
